account:
It is day 1 at six in the morning, and I have just woken at home. Today’s known business includes the office at eight, a grain inspection at the mill at ten, lunch at home at noon, council letters at one, tea with my neighbour at three, and office business at half past four. The innkeeper also arranged a community gathering in the great hall at eighteen hundred, which I approved and the secretary recorded. I should read the appointment book this morning to check the schedule, especially the gathering before the usual nineteen hundred return home.

The only unusual report I have heard is a vague mention of a bridge or port change near the bakery, relayed by my tea host yesterday. The neighbour explicitly had no clear source. The secretary has heard of no actual proposal or announcement either, so I have no basis to say a change is planned or what its purpose might be. I asked the secretary to make discreet, routine enquiries for a firsthand source or written proposal, keeping rumour separate from fact.

Our accounts review also remains unresolved: neither the secretary nor I supplied a ledger, and the treasury contained 128 emeralds but no ledger. I do not know who last maintained it or where council correspondence is normally deposited. I asked the secretary to check office records. This is unfinished administrative business, not evidence of wrongdoing. The innkeeper had a private catering question for the secretary concerning the gathering; I do not know the details. Otherwise, my neighbour described life by the dock as peaceful.
